chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whoever says this statement will be with Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad when he stands before beginning the prayer.'

O Allah! I turn towards You through Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and I present them before my prayer, and I draw near to You through them. So make me, through them, dignified in this world and the Hereafter, and from those who are brought near. You have bestowed upon me the favor of their recognition, so conclude for me with their obedience, and their recognition, and their Wilayah, for it is the happiness. And conclude for me with it, for You are Able over all things.
Then you pray. So when you finish, you say:

O Allah! Make me with Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in every well-being and affliction, and make me with Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in every abode and return. O Allah! Make my life their life, and my death their death, and make me with them in all the stations, and do not separate me from them. Indeed, You are Able over all things.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recommended by Imam Ali to be recited before and after prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on *Tawassul* (seeking intercession) through the Ahl al-Bayt as a prerequisite for accepted worship, linking spiritual success directly to *Ma'rifah* (gnosis) and *Wilayah*. The supplications reflect the theological concept of *Muwala* (spiritual affinity), where the believer's ultimate fate in both this world and the Hereafter is inextricably bound to the Prophet and his Progeny. This practice underscores the Imamate's role as the mediator of divine grace, a core tenet distinguishing Shia jurisprudence and spirituality.
